text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and searching for pagination code.
The bug is visible: `end = start + page_size - 1` makes the slice exclude one item per page. Let me confirm by running the tests.

The test confirms the off-by-one. With 11 items and page size 5, page 1 returns `[1..4]`, page 2 returns `[6..9]`, and page 3 returns `[11]`. Item 5 and item 10 never appear on any page, which matches the "same items, regular interval" symptom in the report.

args.root_cause: In `paginate()`, the slice end index is computed as `end = start + page_size - 1`, but Python slice ends are exclusive, so each page drops its last item. Every page returns `page_size - 1` items, and the item at each multiple of `page_size` (positions 5, 10, ... in 1-based terms) is skipped on every page. With 11 items and page size 5: page 1 = [1..4], page 2 = [6..9], page 3 = [11]; items 5 and 10 are never returned. The correct end index is `start + page_size`. The `Page.total_items`/`total_pages` logic is correct and is not the cause.

start = (page_number - 1) * page_size
    end = start + page_size - 1
    return Page(
        items=items[start:end],

assert [1, 2, 3, 4] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
